ride-sharing-stage-1.title: The Monolith
ride-sharing-stage-1.description: One server does everything for riders and drivers

nodes.label: Rider's Phone
nodes.explanation: The rider's app — shows nearby drivers on a map and lets you tap 'Request Ride' to get picked up

nodes.label: Driver's Phone
nodes.explanation: The driver's app — sends GPS location every few seconds and receives ride requests from the server

nodes.label: The Server
nodes.explanation: Does everything — receives ride requests, tracks driver locations, finds the nearest available driver, and records completed trips

nodes.label: Database
nodes.explanation: Stores everything in one place: trip history, user profiles, payment records, and right now, driver GPS locations too

ride-sharing-stage-2.title: Splitting Hot and Cold Data
ride-sharing-stage-2.description: Redis handles fast-changing GPS data, database keeps permanent records

nodes.label: Rider's Phone
nodes.explanation: Requests a ride and waits for a driver match — the app doesn't know or care what changed on the backend

nodes.label: Driver's Phone
nodes.explanation: Sends GPS updates every 3 seconds — with 5,000 drivers, that's 1,700 updates per second hitting the system

nodes.label: The Server
nodes.explanation: Matches riders to drivers using optimistic locking — checks availability and assigns in one atomic step so two riders can't grab the same driver

nodes.label: Redis
nodes.explanation: Fast in-memory store for driver locations and availability — handles 100,000+ operations per second because it skips writing to disk. Old locations are simply overwritten by new ones.

nodes.label: Database
nodes.explanation: Now only stores persistent data — trip records, payment history, user profiles. No longer drowning in throwaway GPS writes.

ride-sharing-stage-3.title: Microservices
ride-sharing-stage-3.description: Independent services so a payment bug can't take down ride matching

nodes.label: Rider's Phone
nodes.explanation: Sends ride requests to the Matching Service and receives real-time updates about driver assignment and trip progress

nodes.label: Driver's Phone
nodes.explanation: Sends GPS updates and receives ride assignments — now routed through dedicated services instead of one big server

nodes.label: Matching Service
nodes.explanation: Finds the nearest available driver for each ride request — runs independently so a payment bug can never take down ride matching

nodes.label: Redis
nodes.explanation: Still holds ephemeral driver locations and availability — the Matching Service reads from here to find the nearest driver in microseconds

nodes.label: Message Queue
nodes.explanation: The to-do board connecting all services — when a ride is matched, the event waits here until Payment and Notification services are ready to process it

nodes.label: Notifications
nodes.explanation: Sends push notifications and SMS — 'Your driver is 3 minutes away.' Picks up events from the queue whenever it's ready, even after a brief outage

nodes.label: Database
nodes.explanation: The system of record — stores completed trips, payment history, and user accounts. Each service writes its own data here

nodes.label: Payment Service
nodes.explanation: Handles charges, refunds, and driver payouts. If it slows down, the circuit breaker trips and payments get queued — rides keep going
